subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Wind Engineering: Taming the Invisible Enemy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wind Engineering: Taming the Invisible Enemy.

hook.text: The Great Belt Bridge in Denmark was designed to resist winds of 250 km/h. It opened in 1998.

buildup.text: Modern bridge decks use aerodynamic profiles — streamlined shapes that let wind pass through, not push against.

discovery.text: Wind tunnel tests use scale models to study airflow. Smoke trails reveal how air moves around the deck.

twist.text: Some bridges have tuned mass dampers — heavy pendulums inside towers that swing opposite to the wind's force.

climax.text: Computational fluid dynamics now simulates millions of wind scenarios before a single bolt is placed.

punchline.text: You can't stop the wind. But you can design around it.

quiz.question: How do tuned mass dampers protect bridges from wind?
options: They block wind from reaching the bridge deck surface
Heavy pendulums swing opposite to the wind's force to cancel motion
They vibrate at high frequency to stiffen the structure
